title: Properties of molecular substances
log: 2026-11-01T08:04:32Z match: Claude Haiku 5.5 found no bank point the same, so it is written new

match.reason: The closest bank point explains intermolecular forces and boiling points well, but it says nothing about molecules not conducting electricity, which the brief requires, and the new point is about properties rather than the forces themselves.

draft.title: Properties of molecular substances
card: A molecular substance is made of separate molecules. The atoms within each molecule are held by strong covalent bonds. The molecules are held to each other by much weaker forces.
To melt or boil a molecular substance, only these weak forces between molecules must be overcome. The covalent bonds stay intact. So melting and boiling points are low.
Molecules have no free charged particles. They have no ions, and their electrons stay in bonds or lone pairs. So molecular substances do not conduct electricity as solids or liquids.
Many molecular substances are gases or liquids at room temperature. Solids are often soft and easy to break.
draft.remember: Weak forces between molecules mean low melting points, and no free charges means no conduction.

a.q: Why does a molecular substance such as wax melt at a low temperature?
opts: Only weak forces between molecules must be overcome
The covalent bonds in each molecule are weak
The atoms in each molecule are free to move as ions
Its electrons are free to move through the substance
a.why: Melting separates molecules from each other, which takes little energy because the forces between them are weak. The strong covalent bonds inside the molecules stay intact. Saying the covalent bonds are weak is tempting, but they are not broken when it melts.
a.clue: What is pulled apart when a molecular solid melts?

b.q: Liquid ethanol is tested with a battery and a globe. The globe stays off. What is the best explanation?
opts: It has no free ions or electrons to carry charge
Its covalent bonds block the flow of electricity
Its melting point is too low to conduct
Its molecules are too large to move
b.why: Ethanol is made of molecules, with no ions and no free electrons. Without charged particles able to move, there is no current. Low melting point is a property of such substances, but it does not explain the lack of conduction.
b.clue: Conduction needs charged particles that can move.

a.best: Only weak forces between molecules must be overcome

b.best: It has no free ions or electrons to carry charge
